## Summary

nomad421's note "What follows from the dependency trace in the Riemann Hypothesis proof?"
asks J. L. Nielsen to name the step where the formal proof needs a geometric fact and accepts
the trivial certificate in its place. Nielsen's paper, *The Invalidity of Alpöge's Proposed
Proof of the Riemann Hypothesis* (13 pages, PhilArchive NIEIOT-2), lists in §9 four checks that
would confirm or refute her analysis. Her §10 says that she did not run a compiled dependency
trace. This report runs that trace on the kernel export that the independent checkers accepted,
and gives the result of each check.

- **Nielsen's facts hold in the compiled term.** The four constants she names in check 2,
  `anyGeometry`, `geoDegenerate`, `divXFl` and `x0`, are transitive dependencies of
  `riemannHypothesis`.
- **Nothing reads them.** No declaration in the export eliminates the geometry closure `GeoCl`.
  The lemmas that extract a surface from the real geometry predicate are not in the export.
  The two uses of the `geo` field put it into another certificate.
- **The step that turns the bundle into nonvanishing does not depend on them.**
  `zero_free_all_of_green_v_win` and `every_character_of_green_v_win` have no dependency on the
  four constants. The constants reach the main theorem only through one lemma, which assembles
  the hypothesis bundle and its parameters.

So the geometric route that the names describe is not where the argument is. That is the first
of the two cases in Nielsen's Appendix A, and on that point she is right. The compiled term does
not support her conclusion that the proof is invalid or "does not exist". It contains a checked
derivation whose content is in premises that do not touch the vacuous witnesses. That content
has not been explained by anyone, and the graph shows where to look for it.

## Method

A C program (`tool/rhgraph.c`) reads the export as a stream and keeps the expression DAG
in memory. There are 1,065,214,335 expression nodes. The program walks the type, value and
recursor rules of every declaration that is reachable from the five theorems in `Main.lean`.
It writes one edge for each constant that occurs in a declaration, and one record for each
structure projection (`Expr.proj`).

| Quantity | Value |
|---|---|
| Declaration records | 1,468,418. con-leche reports the same number accepted |
| Kinds | 1,246,110 theorems · 214,241 definitions · 7,969 inductive blocks · 91 opaques · 4 `quot` · 3 axioms |
| Reachable from the five theorems | 1,468,414. The other four are `Nat.lor`, `Nat.xor`, `String.mk`, `String.mk._proof_1` |
| Direct dependency edges | 116,225,516 |
| Projection uses | 88,149 |

The edges were loaded into DuckDB. Each query below is a breadth-first search on the reversed
edges ("which declarations depend on X") or a test for edges into a named constant. A
reference to any name in an inductive block brings in the whole block. This makes the walk
over-approximate, never under-approximate, the true dependencies.

## The dependency graph

![Every path from `riemannHypothesis` to the four vacuous witnesses (red), with the other
premises of the lemma where the paths join. Orange: depends on a vacuous witness. Green: does
not. An arrow points from a declaration to a constant that its term uses directly.](depgraph.svg){width=100%}

| Vacuous witness | Namespace | Dependents | Distance from the main theorem |
|---|---|---|---|
| `anyGeometry` | `GlobalTheory.Mem.Top.Bl` | 31 | 8 |
| `x0` | `GlobalTheory.Mem.Top.DivRec` | 52 | 16 |
| `divXFl` | `Formalism.L2.Geo` | 28 | 20 |
| `geoDegenerate` | `Formalism.L2.Geo` | 53 | 21 |
| union of the four | | 85 | |

Only 85 of 1,468,414 declarations depend on any of the four. All of these dependency paths go
through `UpperTheory.Lit.every_character_of_theta_integrals_local_matching`. When it is removed
from the graph, none of the four can be reached from the main theorem. The paths enter that
lemma through two premises:

- `nonempty_hyps_definite_side_of_closed_bound`, which proves that the hypothesis bundle
  `HypsAlt` is nonempty, and
- `parametersOfDependence`, a definition that fills the geometry parameter with `anyGeometry`.

The other premises of the lemma do not depend on any of the four. These are
`every_character_of_green_v_win`, `green_of_regular`, `VWin`, `ThetaIntegralsAgree`,
`RecTExists` and `boundAtTwoThree_linked_of_recT`. The lemma that concludes nonvanishing from
the bundle, `zero_free_all_of_green_v_win`, also has no such dependency. Neither do
`zeroFreeOn_of_tiedWin_cyc`, `rh_of_every`, `linkDIV_at_words`, `Compl3`, `WordFacts` or
`DivInputsR`.

## Is the content of a certificate ever read?

| Test over the whole export | Result |
|---|---|
| Users of `GeoCl.rec` (elimination of the closure) | none outside the `GeoCl` block |
| Users of `OAt.rec` | none |
| `Expr.proj` on the structure `OAt` | only the projection functions `OAt.geo`, `OAt.lam` |
| Users of `OAt.geo` | `oAt_setDiv` (gives it to `GeoCl.step`) and `divEx_geoCl` (gives it to `geoCl_of`) |
| `geoOf`, `geoOf_surf`, `oAt_geoOf` | not in the export |
| `FrobeniusOrbitPlaceCount` | not in the export |
| `True.rec`, `False.elim` and similar in the 85 dependent declarations | none |

A proof that is used only to build another proof of the same kind carries no information to
the conclusion. Every lemma on the path is uniform in the geometry parameter, so it proves the
same thing when the parameter is `True`.

## Nielsen's four checks

1. **Independent kernel replay.** nanoda accepts the full export (exit 0). con-leche
   master accepts all 1,468,418 declarations, and in comparison mode justifies all five
   statements against the Mathlib-only challenge. lean4lean accepts all 175,187 modules. The
   `lake comparator` run under Lean 4.36.0 has passed the statement comparison and the axiom
   check, and its Lean kernel stages are still running. Nielsen is concerned about Lean 4.33.1
   because of the runtime fixes in 4.34.1. nanoda and con-leche check the exported term without
   any code that Lean 4.33.1 compiled. *Case 2 of her Appendix A ("an artifact") would need
   these independent kernels to be unsound in the same way.*
2. **Dependency walk.** All four constants are in the closure (table above). *This
   confirms her finding at the level of the compiled term.*
3. **The degree equation.** `FrobeniusOrbitPlaceCount` is not in the export. The compiled
   proof does not use the statement that would make `dFl` vanish. *The concern does not
   arise.*
4. **The remaining hypotheses.** The vacuous witnesses inhabit the bundle `HypsAlt`, and the
   consumer never reads its geometry. So the content must be in the premises that do not
   depend on the witnesses, and in the fields of the bundle that are not about geometry. The
   graph names those premises (green in the figure). *This report does not find out what is
   in them, so this check is still open.*

## Assessment

**Nielsen is right that** the geometry predicate is `True`, that the certificate is in
the dependency closure, that the lemmas written to extract geometric content are never used,
and that the height equation holds by `rfl`. The route through geometry and lattice
identification is not the argument that derives the theorem. The source presents that route
by its names, so a reader who follows the names will be misled.

**nomad421 is right that** no step uses the trivial certificate as evidence for a geometric
object. The compiled term confirms this for all 1,468,414 declarations. The rewrite at
`RecBridge.lean:338` and the bound `h5 : Compl3 …` are in the part of the graph that does not
depend on the vacuous witnesses.

**On validity.** In her Appendix A, Nielsen accepts that a term which typechecks is a
derivation of Mathlib's `RiemannHypothesis`. The walk shows that this derivation does not get
its conclusion from the vacuous witnesses. It gets the conclusion from premises that do not
touch them. A geometric route that is presented but not used does not make the derivation
invalid. It means that the mathematical argument has not been written down. That is a real
gap in the exposition, and it should be closed before anyone accepts the result as
understood. It is not a gap in the proof that was checked.

## Limits

- No kernel was run for this report. The acceptance of the export comes from Sutherland's
  runs, and the Comparator kernel stages under Lean 4.36.0 were not complete at the time of
  reading.
- The graph shows which constants a term contains. It does not show how a term uses them.
  A dependency can be on the path and still carry no information. The "never read" findings
  come from the absence of eliminations and projections. They do not come from an analysis
  of each term.
- The green premises do not depend on the four witnesses that Nielsen names. They can contain
  other vacuous definitions. That is the open part of her check 4.
- The claims in Nielsen's §§3–5, about the degenerate model, the lattice witness and the
  two geometries, were not rechecked field by field. The constants they concern are present,
  and the graph shows which declarations reach them.

## Reproduction

```sh
curl -LO https://math.mit.edu/~drew/grh/solution.ndjson.zst      # 7.7 GB
gcc -O2 -o rhgraph tool/rhgraph.c
zstd -dc --long=31 solution.ndjson.zst | ./rhgraph out riemannHypothesis \
  riemannZeta_eq_zero_re LFunction_ne_zero_of_half_lt_re \
  LFunction_eq_zero_re LFunction_eq_zero_re_of_isPrimitive       # about 10 min, 60 GB RAM
# load out/{names,closure,edges,projs}.tsv into DuckDB; tool/anc.sh computes dependents
```
